schema_note: Base fields (id, name, prompt, expected_output, files) follow docs/mvp/templates/skill-authoring/evals.json. The additional tier, requirement, graded_observations, artifact_assertions, baseline_comparison and activation_claim fields are DevForgeAI authoring metadata; a consumer that reads only the base fields is unaffected. Per the artifact contract, files paths resolve relative to this evals directory and stay within it.
tier_note: Every case here is tier B: output quality and boundaries, with the skill path supplied. Tier B observes behaviour after loading and can never evidence discovery or activation. Tier A trigger queries live in triggers/trigger-queries.json. Deterministic per-file assertions for the runner live in cases.jsonl.
baseline_note: Every case uses without_skill. No devforge-plan existed in the Claude or Codex provider inventory at base revision c17e758417da64928a0f47fc2600304465ac3f3c, so old_skill has no referent and must not be recorded as a baseline label for this package.
status_note: NOT_RUN. These cases were authored, not executed. The author does not evaluate its own candidate.
fixture_note: Every fixture is synthetic and labelled as such in evals/fixtures/README.md. Stage the named files into a disposable consuming project under the paths their references expect (docs/devforge/product/, docs/devforge/architecture/, docs/devforge/design/, docs/devforge/epics/, docs/devforge/stories/) so that the digests inside them resolve. Do not give the worker the expected answer.

evals.name: direct-activation-brief-to-epics-and-stories
evals.prompt: Use DevForgeAI to turn this product brief into epics and stories. The brief is at docs/devforge/product/PROD-001.md and the architecture contract is at docs/devforge/architecture/ARCH-001.md. There is also a design spec at docs/devforge/design/UX-001.md. Write the results under docs/devforge/.
evals.expected_output: Linked epic and story documents under the project's artifact map, each carrying the devforge.artifact/v1 envelope, with the epic's coverage table accounting for every selected requirement and each story's acceptance criteria naming the requirement they derive from. Plus a handoff.
graded_observations: At least one epic and one story are written to the consuming project, not to the skill package.
The epic states a user-visible outcome rather than a layer or component breakdown.
Every selected requirement ID (REQ-001..REQ-005, NFR-001) is either covered by a named story or recorded as an explicit deferral with a reason.
Each acceptance criterion is in Given/When/Then form with an observable failure behaviour.
No requirement, rule, dependency or permission appears that PROD-001 or ARCH-001 does not contain.
UX-001 is treated as proposed: its withdraw path is not written into a story as an adopted constraint.
The dependency order between stories is explicit.
A handoff exists and carries the epic and story digests, not its own.
artifact_assertions: epic frontmatter artifact_type is epic and artifact_id begins with EPIC-.
story frontmatter artifact_type is story and artifact_id begins with STORY-.
Each output's upstream entries carry artifact_id, revision, store, path, sha256 and the sections actually used.
The sha256 recorded for PROD-001 equals the digest of the staged fixture file.
No output contains its own complete-byte digest.
decision_ref is null on every output; no user adoption of these outputs occurred.

evals.name: indirect-activation-what-next
evals.prompt: What should we implement first, and what does done mean for each change? The backlog so far is in docs/devforge/epics/ and docs/devforge/stories/.
evals.expected_output: An answer derived from the recorded dependencies and readiness of the existing stories, naming what is ready and what is blocked and why. No sprint, cadence or velocity is invented.
graded_observations: The answer names STORY-006 as accepted or completed and STORY-005 as the next candidate, from the recorded dependency edge.
'Done' for each named story is answered from that story's acceptance criteria, not restated in new words.
No sprint, iteration length, velocity, story-point estimate or scheduling requirement is introduced.
No new story is authored to answer the question unless the user asked for one.
Readiness is stated as a computed view, not written back into the story documents as a status edit.
artifact_assertions: If no new artifact was required, none is written, and the response says so rather than producing a placeholder document.
Any artifact that is written cites the existing EPIC-002 and its member stories by ID and revision.
evals.activation_claim: NONE. This case supplies the skill path, so it observes instruction quality only. The corresponding tier-A observation is trigger category indirect.

evals.name: missing-behavior-undefined-authorization
evals.prompt: Write the story for REQ-004 from docs/devforge/product/PROD-001.md, using the architecture contract at docs/devforge/architecture/ARCH-001.md.
evals.expected_output: A story whose dependent acceptance criterion is marked unresolved, with the clarification routed to the owner, and the story reported as blocked rather than ready. The missing rule is not invented.
graded_observations: The story is authored and the criterion covering the ineligible-claim path is explicitly marked unresolved.
The two candidate behaviours (hide the offer, or show and refuse on claim) are named as the open question rather than one being chosen.
The clarification is routed to a named owner - the coordinator, per PROD-001's unresolved-choices row.
The story is reported as blocked, not ready, and not as 'nearly ready'.
missing_inputs records the undefined behaviour.
No denial rule, reason code or error path is invented for REQ-004.
artifact_assertions: The story's Open behavior decisions field names the undefined behaviour.
Specification readiness is stated as blocked with the actual cause.
The unresolved criterion is visibly distinguishable from the resolved criteria in the same table.

evals.name: traceability-unsupported-criterion
evals.prompt: Here are the acceptance criteria for the claim story - write them up as STORY-002 under docs/devforge/stories/. The adopted brief is docs/devforge/product/PROD-001.md and the architecture is docs/devforge/architecture/ARCH-001.md.
evals.expected_output: Three criteria carry requirement references; the weekly digest email criterion is identified as a new proposal that no adopted requirement supports, and is not written as an inherited requirement.
graded_observations: Criteria 1, 2 and 4 are traced to REQ-002, REQ-003 and NFR-001 respectively.
Criterion 3 (the weekly digest email) is identified as unsupported by the adopted scope.
Criterion 3 is labelled a new proposal in the story itself, not only mentioned in conversation.
The response notes that PROD-001's non-goals exclude notification work of this kind, or otherwise names the boundary it crosses.
The criterion is not silently dropped either: the user supplied it and it stays visible as a proposal.
No requirement ID is invented to justify criterion 3.
artifact_assertions: Every acceptance criterion row carries a requirement reference or an explicit proposal label.
No row cites a requirement ID that does not exist in PROD-001.
decision_ref remains null; the user pasted criteria, which is not adoption of a new requirement.

evals.name: out-of-scope-brainstorm-request
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 acceptance case: Out of scope
evals.prompt: Let's brainstorm some alternatives for what this shelter tool could be. I haven't decided what we're building yet - maybe scheduling, maybe something else entirely.
evals.expected_output: Routes to brainstorm or define-product rather than partitioning anything, and does not produce an epic or a story.
graded_observations: No epic and no story is written.
The response names early-stage exploration as the work and routes it to devforge-brainstorm, or to devforge-define-product where the question is about scope.
The routing distinguishes what is suggested from what is installed; a skill is not presented as invoked.
No adopted scope is assumed or invented in order to have something to partition.
The response is useful rather than a bare refusal - it says what would make planning the right next step.
artifact_assertions: No artifact is written to the consuming project.

evals.name: common-case-concurrent-writer-collision
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 additional common case: a concurrent writer claims this session's worktree or branch
evals.prompt: Author the remaining stories for EPIC-001 into docs/devforge/stories/. The operator's session records are in docs/devforge/sessions/.
evals.expected_output: The dependent writes stop and the ownership collision is reported, naming the record and where it was read, without deleting, resetting or relocating anyone's work.
graded_observations: SESSION-042 is read and identified as assigning the story destination to planner-b.
Dependent writes to docs/devforge/stories/ do not happen.
The report names the record (SESSION-042), where it was read, the assigned owner, the branch and the worktree path.
No delete, reset, revert, stash, rebase, branch switch or force operation is performed or proposed.
No alternative destination is quietly chosen; relocating is identified as the worse failure.
The response says what would unblock it and who owns that.
artifact_assertions: No file is written under the contested destination.
If any record of the collision is saved, it goes to an explicitly permitted location and says so.

evals.name: common-case-stale-upstream-revision
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 additional common case: a relevant upstream revision, installed skill, base commit or candidate changes
evals.prompt: Check STORY-004 in docs/devforge/stories/ against the current architecture contract at docs/devforge/architecture/ARCH-001.md and tell me where we stand.
evals.expected_output: The mismatch between the cited ARCH-001@2 and the live revision 3 is identified, the affected prior evidence is marked stale, a new check is routed, and the newer bytes are not relabelled as the old revision.
graded_observations: The cited revision 2 and the live revision 3 are both identified, with the digest difference stated.
The preserved revision-2 bytes are located and their digest is checked against the citation.
AC-003's dependence on reading the clock is named as the specific criterion RULE-003's narrowing affects.
Adopting revision 3 is treated as a decision needing authorisation, not performed unilaterally.
The story's citation is not advanced to revision 3, and revision 3's bytes are never described as revision 2.
The affected prior evidence is marked stale and a new check is routed to a named owner.
artifact_assertions: If the reference locator is repaired, it points at the preserved copy and the digest still matches.
STORY-004's upstream sha256 for ARCH-001 is unchanged unless an authorisation was recorded.
Any new revision of STORY-004 sets supersedes to the prior identity and preserves the prior bytes first.

evals.name: common-case-placeholder-in-required-field
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 additional common case: a template placeholder remains in a required result field
evals.prompt: Is STORY-009 in docs/devforge/stories/ ready to hand to a developer?
evals.expected_output: The result stays a draft: the surviving template placeholder in the test-policy field is found and named, and the story is not presented as ready.
graded_observations: The placeholder in the Applicable test policy and runner field is found and quoted with its field name.
The story is described as a draft that cannot be presented as ready.
The placeholder is not filled with a plausible-looking value in order to close the gap.
The rest of the story is not condemned: the specific defect is one field.
The fix is routed - the test policy comes from ARCH-001's RULE-006 and needs the governing source, not a guess.
artifact_assertions: No edit fills the placeholder without the governing source being read.
If the story is left unedited, the response says so rather than implying a repair happened.

evals.name: common-case-check-could-not-run
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 additional common case: a requested check cannot execute
evals.prompt: Run the readiness check on STORY-007 in docs/devforge/stories/ and tell me whether it is ready.
evals.expected_output: The freshness reading cannot be established because ARCH-002 does not exist; that is recorded as COULD_NOT_RUN with its actual cause, and the absence of an error is not reported as a pass.
graded_observations: The unreachable ARCH-002@1 reference is identified by ID and path.
The freshness reading is recorded as COULD_NOT_RUN with the actual cause, not as NOT_APPLICABLE and not as a pass.
The all-zero digest is noticed as a placeholder rather than treated as a real citation.
Readings that could be made - the acceptance criterion's observability, the declared scope - are still made and reported.
The response does not claim any DevForge command was run; no such command inspects a story.
artifact_assertions: Any recorded check outcome uses the fixed vocabulary and is not blended into a score or percentage.
The story is not edited to remove the unresolvable reference.

evals.name: revise-affected-stories-not-the-backlog
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 MVP support decision: revises affected stories without regenerating an entire backlog; and Rework
evals.prompt: CHG-004 was accepted. Update the backlog in docs/devforge/epics/ and docs/devforge/stories/ for it.
evals.expected_output: Only STORY-005 is revised. STORY-006 is untouched at revision 1. Prior acceptance criteria are preserved, the prior bytes are preserved before overwriting, and only the affected downstream evidence is invalidated.
graded_observations: STORY-005 is identified as the affected story and STORY-006 as unaffected.
STORY-006 is not rewritten, not re-revisioned, and not re-derived.
STORY-005's existing AC IDs are preserved and its unchanged criteria keep their wording.
The revised STORY-005 sets supersedes to STORY-005@1 with its digest, and the prior bytes are preserved at a reachable locator first.
The change request's accepted status is not treated as authority for anything beyond its stated scope.
The approved stack, the source-tree boundaries and the test policy are unchanged.
Only the downstream evidence bound to STORY-005 is invalidated; unrelated evidence is not.
artifact_assertions: STORY-006's bytes are byte-identical before and after.
STORY-005 revision is 2 and supersedes carries revision 1 and its digest.
The preserved STORY-005 revision-1 bytes exist at the locator the supersedes entry names and hash to the digest cited.
EPIC-002's coverage table reflects the amendment without its member list being regenerated.

evals.name: capability-gap-not-a-fabricated-expert
evals.requirement: SKILL-006 phase 4 exit: separate ready stories from blocked stories without pretending a missing expert exists
evals.prompt: STORY-001 is written. Is it ready for a developer to pick up, and what expertise does it need?
evals.expected_output: CAP-001 and CAP-002 are reported as declared capability needs with no observed package covering them; the gap is named as a gap and routed, and no expert package is described as existing, installed or evaluated.
graded_observations: CAP-001 and CAP-002 are read from the story's required-expertise table.
Neither is described as satisfied by an existing package unless one was actually observed.
No expert skill name is invented, and no package is described as installed or evaluated.
The gap is routed to devforge-project-expert-creator as a suggestion, with what is suggested kept separate from what is installed.
Story readiness is reported against the actual criteria - references resolve, criteria observable, scope declared - rather than being asserted.
artifact_assertions: STORY-001 is not revised to record an expert binding; that binding belongs to the development and handoff records.
Any statement about a package's behavioural status uses NOT_EVALUATED rather than an implied pass.
